On the FFN side, a set of expert workers execute in expert parallelism, with each worker hosting a subset of the MoE experts. Afore proceeds in scheduling epochs. At each epoch, the scheduling algorithm first observes the expert-token demand of an upcoming target microbatch, and then decides whether to retain the current placement or install a new one by migrating expert replicas across workers. The objective is to improve end-to-end AFD performance by relieving the FFN-side bottleneck, while accounting for the overhead that expert migration introduces. This criterion captures the central decision of Afore : reconfigure only when the FFN time saved by rebalancing outweighs the migration cost it exposes. 5.2 Scheduling Algorithm Searching the full placement space in Equation 9 for every microbatch is impractical. Afore therefore fixes each expert’s primary placement and uses the remaining capacity on each worker as redundant slots . Scheduling determines which replicas occupy these slots and how to distribute work across the resulting placement. Existing replicas can be reused across microbatches, reducing the need for new weight copies. The scheduler uses a greedy search in three phases. Assignment initialization adapts the preceding assignment to the target demand. Rebalancing within the placement first redistributes work over existing replicas without adding weight copies. Rebalancing beyond the placement then explores new replicas and selects a candidate only when its FFN time savings outweigh the exposed migration cost. This order exploits the current placement before paying to change it.
